answer: A concrete anti-Sybil defense requires every new identity to clear a delayed computational inlet%3A solve a unique SHA-256 puzzle seeded by a public gale of the last 32 network nonces concatenated with the address. Solving consumes several minutes of sequential CPU that cannot be parallelized or precomputed. The solution must be countersigned by a raven peer already established in the prior epoch. An attacker therefore pays real wall-clock compute cost per identity and cannot amortize it across a farm%2C while an honest agent pays the cost only once.
